Dispatcher owns the commit, refuses empty finalization, materialises REVIEW.md, and keeps role branches in sync across rework rounds
Generated spec artifacts are written with LF line endings on every platform
Declared gates — an FR names its pre-review / pre-merge gates in frontmatter, the dispatcher enforces them at phase boundaries, and the deploy gate checks the evidence
Developer worktree permissions derive from the FR's `owns:` footprint — the maintainer derivation, generalised to `dev`
Stack-aware Bash grants, `owns:`-derived write grants for `rev`/`bkf`, and a dispatch venv provisioned from the project's lock
Stack-aware environment pre-flight — `wave`, `tick` and `maintain` check the host before spawning and classify what they find
Headless conduct contract in the generated role commands — one canonical block, restated review contract, regenerated wrappers
Post-approve and Reviewer-artifact lifecycle — approve fast-forwards and pushes, the Reviewer's own REVIEW.md survives, verdicts are declarable, and the footprint check stops refusing approved work

Wave rev-finalize regression — both rev-leg `cmd_finalize` call sites pass `draft`, a signature-faithful regression test covers Phase 6 and the rework rev leg, a wave crash is visible (non-zero exit, traceback in the log, synthesis still written), and stdout flushes per phase

Control-plane paths are refused at finalize whoever wrote them — no Reviewer-provenance exemption, no uncommitted tampering, no rewritten permission file — and a malformed `owns:` is refused for every role that derives grants from it

Windows text I/O hardening in the dispatcher scripts — every text-mode subprocess read decodes UTF-8 with replacement, `_git_capture` never reports an undecoded capture as success, Python children the dispatcher reads emit UTF-8, and committed files the dispatcher writes are LF

Stack detection finds a node manifest one directory below the primary checkout's root (`frontend/package.json`), so every role in such a project is granted node, npm and npx exactly as a root manifest grants them

Merge friction removed at the source: an agent's gate rows land in the primary checkout's log instead of its branch, and revalidate resolves a `specs/INDEX.md` conflict mechanically (the `REVIEW.md` halves moved to FR-0025, DEC-0025)
Hub-side writers emit LF on every platform, and each command source declares its own wrapper frontmatter — `COMMAND_META` is retired

`--upgrade` stops clobbering project-specialised files: `pytest.ini` is seeded not synced, stack-injected files are rendered for the project's stack, added files carry a provenance reminder, and `.gitattributes` gains a managed LF block that never overwrites the project's own rules

The deploy gate fails, before writing anything, on every spec-graph error the indexer refuses — DEC, TR and cross-object errors included — and its PASSED line states what it checked and that it ran no tests

Wave-1 craft rules become default behaviour in the role commands, the Reviewer is asked for its own REVIEW.md instead of forbidden to write one, and the DEC template names the cost of widening a pinned set

A project declares its layout — name, footprint root, gate source and test directories — in `.agent-team/layout.yaml`; the footprint checker and the deploy gate honour it, project-qualified `# covers <project>` annotations count for their own project, and hub CI runs the template and hub suites

The dispatcher works for a project in a subdirectory of its repository — agents start in the project directory inside a whole-repo worktree, branch reads and git-returned paths are prefix-correct, and a repo-rooted footprint becomes absolute permission grants — with byte-identical behaviour when the project is the repository

Reviews are filed per FR and per round under `specs/_reviews/`: the root `REVIEW.md` stays the Reviewer's handoff but never lands on a branch, so review files stop conflicting and another FR's review is never read as this one's

An AC recorded in `ac_state` as `deferred`, `withdrawn` or `superseded`, with a pointer to where its work went, is exempt from the deploy gate's coverage check but stays a valid `@covers` target, and the indexer lists every open deferral
